Women's World Cup all-time top scorers

By Olive · Updated 2026-11-25

Brazil's Marta is the all-time top scorer at the FIFA Women's World Cup, with 17 goals in 23 matches across six tournaments. Birgit Prinz of Germany and Abby Wambach of the United States share second place on 14 goals, and Michelle Akers of the United States is fourth with 12. The totals on this page run to the end of the most recent tournament, in 2023.

Two of the seven are Brazilian, the team hosting the 2027 tournament. The United States and Germany also have two players each on the list.

Goals per match

Scoring rates differ more than the totals suggest. For the players whose match counts we could confirm:

Marta17230.74

Marta's 23 matches include the 2023 tournament, her sixth. Many older lists give her 20 matches, which was her total before 2023.

Other scoring records

  • Most goals at one tournament: 10, by Michelle Akers at the first Women's World Cup in 1991.
  • Most goals in one match: 5. Akers did it first, in 1991, and Alex Morgan of the United States matched it against Thailand in 2019.

What this means for 2027

The 2027 Women's World Cup will be played in Brazil from 24 June to 25 July 2027, the first edition in South America. This page does not try to predict who might add to their total there. For the teams that have qualified so far, see qualified teams; for dates and venues, see the match schedule.

How we checked these numbers

The totals for the top four, Marta's matches and tournaments, and both scoring records are checked against FIFA's own articles. The other totals and match counts come from the sports data company Opta and at least one independent news outlet that gives the same figure; if two sources disagreed on a number, we left it out. The sources below show which check each number passed.
